session: Topic 1 - Functions of one variable and graphs
bullets: Focus on polynomial, exponential and logarithmic functions and their properties; also types of functions, graphs and inverse functions.
Quadratic ax²+bx+c=0: x = (-b ± √(b²-4ac)) / 2a (used in midterm Q1 and Q8).
Exponential equations: write both sides with the same base, then equate exponents. Midterm: 5^(x²+2x-6)=25=5² gives x²+2x-8=0, x=2 or -4.
Log rules: ln(x^k)=k·ln(x), and ln x = c means x = e^c. Midterm: 3ln(x⁴)+3ln(x²)=54 gives 18 ln x = 54, x = e³.
Inverse functions undo each other (exp and ln are inverses).
Applications are economic: demand P = 400 - 4Q can be inverted to Q = 100 - P/4.
examTip: Show every step (the midterm asked for clear steps, 3 decimals). Common slip: forgetting to bring the power down from ln(x^k) or dropping the second quadratic root.

bullets: Syllabus lists limits as a single topic; it feeds directly into the derivative definition.
Limit at infinity of a ratio of polynomials of equal degree = ratio of the leading coefficients.
Method: keep only the highest power in numerator and denominator when x→±∞ (or divide by the highest power).
Lower-order terms (20x², x, -600) become negligible as |x| grows.
examTip: Likely a limit at infinity of a rational function. Common mistake: ignoring the sign of the leading coefficients (answer was negative).

bullets: Syllabus: slopes and curves, tangents and derivatives, sum, product, ratio and composition (chain) rules, higher-order derivatives, derivatives of exp and ln.
Power rule: d/dx x^n = n·x^(n-1); √(x³)=x^(3/2) so f'(x)=(3/2)x^(1/2). Midterm Q4: f'(16)=6.
Tangent line at x=a: y - f(a) = f'(a)(x - a). Midterm: f(16)=64, slope 6, so y = 6x - 32.
Quotient rule: (u/v)' = (u'v - uv') / v². Midterm Q5: f(x)=(2x-5)/ln x, f'(2) ≈ 3.926.
Product rule: (uv)' = u'v + uv'. Midterm Q8: f=(x²-15)e^x gives f'=e^x(x²+2x-15).
d/dx e^x = e^x and d/dx ln x = 1/x. Second derivative f'' is the derivative of f'.
Economic use: elasticity εd = (dQ/dP)(P/Q); midterm Q6 gave εd = -1 at P=200 (Q=50).
examTip: Expect product/quotient rule calculations and a tangent line. Common mistake: wrong sign in the quotient rule numerator, or forgetting to evaluate at the given x.

bullets: Syllabus: simple tests for extreme points, extreme value theorem, local extreme points, inflection points, applications.
First-order condition: f'(x)=0 gives critical points. Midterm Q8: e^x(x+5)(x-3)=0 gives x=-5 or 3.
First-derivative test: f' changes + to - means local max; - to + means local min. Midterm: x=-5 local max, x=3 local min.
Second-derivative test: f''<0 means max (concave), f''>0 means min (convex). Midterm Q7: f''(1)=6a-1>0 so a>1/6.
Profit: TP = TR - TC. Midterm Q9: TP = -5Q²+100Q-72, TP'=0 gives Q=10, TP''=-10<0, max profit 428.
Revenue: TR = P·Q, MR = dTR/dQ, AR = TR/Q. Midterm Q6: TR=400Q-4Q², MR=400-8Q, AR=400-4Q.
Inflection points are where concavity changes (f'' changes sign).
examTip: Applied profit/revenue maximisation is likely: derive TP, set TP'=0, justify with TP''. Common mistake: skipping the second-order justification or mixing up TR, MR and AR.

bullets: Syllabus: antiderivatives and the constant of integration, basic rules, polynomial/exponential/log integrals.
Also listed: integration by substitution, integration by parts, definite integrals.
Definite integrals give area under a curve and between curves; applications follow.
Integration reverses differentiation: if F'(x)=f(x) then ∫f dx = F(x) + C.
This topic starts the part of the final worth about 80% together with Topics 6-9 (final is ~20% Topics 1-4).
examTip: Not covered in the midterm material, so expect it on the final. Common mistake: forgetting +C on indefinite integrals or the limits on definite ones.

bullets: Syllabus motivation: production, profit, utility and cost functions depend on several variables.
Functions of two variables: domain and graph (surfaces).
Level curves (contour plots) show where f(x,y) is constant.
Partial derivatives: differentiate with respect to one variable, treat the others as constants; interpret as marginal effects.
Gradient: vector of partial derivatives, points in the direction of steepest increase.
Practical applications in economics and business.
examTip: Expect computing partial derivatives and gradients and interpreting them. Common mistake: differentiating the 'constant' variable too.

bullets: Critical points of f(x,y): solve the system of first-order conditions f_x=0 and f_y=0.
Second-order partial derivatives are collected in the Hessian matrix.
Use the Hessian to classify critical points: local maximum, local minimum or saddle point.
Basic concepts of convexity and concavity for functions of several variables.
Applications in economics and business (e.g. profit with two products).
examTip: Likely: solve the FOC system, build the Hessian and classify. Common mistake: solving the system wrongly or misreading the sign test.

bullets: Motivation: decisions face constraints (budget, resources).
Equality-constrained optimization can be solved by substitution (plug the constraint into the objective).
Lagrange multipliers: build the Lagrangian L = f - λ(g - c) and set all partial derivatives to zero.
The multiplier λ has an economic meaning: the shadow price of the constraint.
Applications: budget allocation, production planning, portfolio selection.
examTip: Expect a Lagrange or substitution problem plus interpretation of λ. Common mistake: forgetting to include the constraint equation in the system.

bullets: Syllabus: factorials, permutations, arrangements, combinations, and applications.
Factorial: n! = n(n-1)...1.
Order matters means permutation/arrangement; order does not matter means combination.
Choose the right counting tool before computing.
Also called elementary counting techniques and sequences in the course objectives.
examTip: Decide first whether order matters. Common mistake: using combinations when order matters (or the reverse).
